items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And of course Tommy had Charlie Shavers writing in his band

ctx.x: I want to ask you a question about jazz. You know we had talked, and you had talked about this too, how that in the early years of jazz of course before a certain time, like before Benny Goodman, all the bands were pretty much segregated, and then he began to hire Lionel Hampton and Teddy Wilson. But it seemed to me that the music was the one thing that allowed people to go back and forth without all these barriers, you know? Do you see a way that we can use music today to do the same things? Because it seems to…

Be integrated more? Yeah, it should be. Well you know they have it in the smaller groups they don’t have the big bands really to mix it more, with more, because we don’t have big bands. But that’s one thing that they never paid much attention to, you know? Of course © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-

Benny would do what he wanted to do, and so did Jimmy, Jimmy Dorsey. He had a girl named, black girl named June Richmond and boy she could sing, boy. And he brought her from California all through Texas and everywhere with him. So you’ve got to give him credit for that. This was Jimmy, not Tommy, Jimmy, his brother, you know? And of course Tommy had Charlie Shavers writing in his band, and Sy Oliver was writing all these arrangements. So there was more integration, more. Of course we had more musicians and as I…
